content: 1. For immunocompetent hosts, the preferred regimen includes Ampicillin-Sulbactam at a dose of 2 grams administered intravenously every 4 hours. Alternatively, Clindamycin at 600 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours can also be used. 2. For immunocompromised hosts, the preferred regimens are as follows: Cefotaxime at 2 grams intravenously every 6 hours. Ceftizoxime at 4 grams intravenously every 8 hours. Piperacillin at 3 grams intravenously every 4 hours. Imipenem at 500 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours. Meropenem at 1 gram intravenously every 8 hours. Gatifloxacin at 400 milligrams intravenously every 24 hours. 3. In cases of acute laryngitis, the use of antibiotics is not associated with significant improvement in objective symptoms and is not indicated for treatment. 4. For diphtheria, the CDC recommends: Erythromycin, either orally or intravenously, for 14 days at a dose of 40 milligrams per kilogram per day, with a maximum of 2 grams per day. Alternatively, Procaine Penicillin G can be administered intramuscularly for 14 days at a dose of 300,000 units per day for patients weighing less than 10 kilograms. 5. For sinusitis in pediatric patients with treatment failure, a culture should be performed, and treatment should be adjusted accordingly. In the absence of cultures, or for children failing Amoxicillin, the following regimens are recommended: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate (extra strength) suspension at 90 milligrams per kilogram per day (Amoxicillin component) orally, divided every 12 hours for 10–14 days. If Amoxicillin-Clavulanate fails, Clindamycin at 30–40 milligrams per kilogram per day divided every 8 hours, combined with a third-generation cephalosporin such as Cefuroxime Axetil at 30 milligrams per kilogram per day orally, divided every 12 hours. Preferred regimens include Cefdinir at 14 milligrams per kilogram per day orally, divided every 12 or 24 hours, or Cefpodoxime at 10 milligrams per kilogram per day orally, divided every 12 hours. 6. For adult sinusitis with treatment failure after 7 days of diagnosis, the preferred regimens are: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate at 4 grams per day (Amoxicillin equivalent). Levofloxacin at 500 milligrams orally once daily. Moxifloxacin at 400 milligrams orally once daily. 7. For stomatitis: Aphthous stomatitis may benefit from topical steroids to reduce pain and swelling. Herpetic stomatitis can be treated with Acyclovir at 15 milligrams per kilogram orally every 5 hours for 7 days. 8. For submandibular space infections, including Ludwig’s angina, the causative pathogens often include Viridans streptococci, Peptostreptococcus, Bacteroides, and other oral anaerobes. The preferred regimens for immunocompetent hosts are: Penicillin G at 2–4 million units intravenously every 4–6 hours combined with Tobramycin at 2 milligrams per kilogram intravenously every 8 hours. Alternatively, Ampicillin-Sulbactam at 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours, Clindamycin at 600 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours, Doxycycline at 200 milligrams intravenously every 12 hours, Cefotetan at 2 grams intravenously every 12 hours, or Cefotaxime at 2 grams intravenously every 6 hours. 9. For tonsillitis, the preferred regimen is Penicillin V orally for 10 days. If compliance is unlikely, a single dose of Benzathine Penicillin intramuscularly can be administered. Alternative regimens include: Second-generation cephalosporins orally for 4–6 days. Clindamycin or Azithromycin for 5 days. Clarithromycin for 10 days. Erythromycin for 10 days.
